title: From Score Matrices to Football-Aware Match-State Simulation: An Auditable LLM Harness for Exact-Score Reranking

lora_training_pair.instruction: Compare the four documented iterations of the football exact-score forecasting harness and report the Top-1 accuracy, Top-3 accuracy, and candidate coverage achieved by the strongest iteration on the chronological replay benchmark.
lora_training_pair.input: The paper describes V1 as a dynamic score-driven Dixon-Coles baseline, V2 as an LLM contextual-rating mapping into expected-goal parameters, V3 as goal-by-goal simulation over a frozen score-candidate set, and V4 as a version adding shared first-breakthrough and post-goal cascade judgments, time-aware stopping, and deterministic tail candidates. The benchmark is the first 150 matches of the 2025-26 English Premier League.
lora_training_pair.output: V4 was the strongest iteration on the benchmark, reaching 14.7% Top-1 exact-score accuracy and 30.7% Top-3 exact-score accuracy. It increased candidate coverage to 84.7%. For comparison, V1 achieved 10.0% Top-1 and 26.7% Top-3, while V3 achieved 12.0% Top-1 and 30.0% Top-3. The paper characterizes these results as exploratory rather than an untouched benchmark, because the development slice was not fully held out and temporal input isolation could not rule out outcome memory in a closed LLM.

summary: The paper presents an auditable hybrid architecture for football exact-score forecasting that combines dynamic Poisson-family score models with LLM-based contextual reasoning. It documents four iterations: a Dixon-Coles baseline, expected-goal parameter correction from LLM ratings, goal-by-goal simulation, and a final version incorporating first-breakthrough and post-goal cascade judgments, time-aware stopping, and deterministic tail candidates. On the first 150 matches of the 2025-26 English Premier League, V4 achieved 14.7% Top-1 and 30.7% Top-3 exact-score accuracy and raised candidate coverage to 84.7%. The paper also reports V1 native 1X2 metrics of 53.3% argmax accuracy, 0.9878 log loss, 0.5870 Brier score, and 0.2095 ranked probability score. The authors describe the benchmark as exploratory and note limitations involving development-slice contamination and possible outcome memory in a closed LLM.

key_data_points.value: Benchmark: chronological replay of the first 150 matches of the 2025-26 English Premier League
V4 candidate coverage: 84.7%, up from V1's 77.3%
V1 native 1X2 log loss: 0.9878; Brier score: 0.5870; ranked probability score: 0.2095

Dynamic Poisson-family models estimate team strength, expected goals, and coherent score probabilities, but do not directly understand roles, tactical matchups, motivation, or how a first goal changes behaviour.
